subject: Staggered SLO phasing & regional observation proposal
messages:
From: Alice Gomez <alice.gomez@finco.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@finco.com
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API p50/p95 measurement windows — need proposal for phased targets

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the demo earlier this week. Our security and procurement teams are aligned on moving forward, but they want a concrete plan for how Redwood will commit to p50/p95 targets during the onboarding period. Specifically:

- We need an interim set of targets for the first 30–60 days while we ramp traffic and complete validation.
- We require region-specific measurement windows (EU first, then global).
- Clarity on how you compute p95 (rolling windows, sampling, carve-outs for cache warmup).

I've attached our RFQ (FinCo-SLO-RFQ.docx). Can you send a short proposal that includes interim numbers, measurement windows, and any evidence we can present to our compliance team?

Also include how credits or remediation will be handled if you miss the target during the phased period.

Best,
Alice
Alice Gomez
Head of Platform Ops — FinCo Payments

From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: Alice Gomez <alice.gomez@finco.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API p50/p95 measurement windows — need proposal for phased targets
Attachments: redwood-staggered-slo-proposal.pdf

Hi Alice —

Appreciate the clear ask and the RFQ. I've attached a short proposal that outlines a staged approach we typically recommend for larger onboards:

Proposal (high level)
- Phase 0 (validation, days 0–7): monitoring only — 7-day rolling window for observations; no contractual credits.
- Phase 1 (interim, days 8–30): interim contractual targets with regional stagger (EU only). Monitoring: 7-day rolling for operations; contractual evaluation: 30-day contiguous window for p95.
- Phase 2 (tighten, day 31+): move to standard production targets once traffic and telemetry stabilize.

Suggested interim numbers (example for hosted text-generation workload):
- Interim: p50 = 100 ms, p95 = 600 ms (EU region, days 8–30)
- Production: p50 = 70 ms, p95 = 450 ms (goal once warmed and telemetry validated)

Important measurement notes (see appendix in PDF):
- p95 computed over request-level latencies across a 30-day evaluation window for contractual purposes; operational alerts use 7-day rolling percentiles and sample windows.
- We apply a short cache-warmup carve-out (first 10 minutes after deploy or model switch) and exclude known maintenance windows captured in our status page.
- Credits: during Phase 1 we propose a capped remediation credit schedule (pro-rated, not full SLA credit) — details in the PDF.

If you’re comfortable, we can loop in product/infra to align on exact calculation and add the proposal as an addendum to the contract. Next steps: internal alignment and quick call with Karthik/Ben to confirm measurement method.

Thanks — sending to procurement as well.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Hosted API p50/p95 measurement windows — FinCo ask (need quick alignment)

Team — forwarding FinCo's request and my draft proposal. TL;DR: they want interim contractual numbers for the first 30 days, EU-first rollout, and clarity on measurement rules (rolling vs contiguous windows).

Questions for infra/ops:
1) Are the carve-outs I listed (10 min deploy warmup, maintenance windows) sufficient and auditable?
2) For contractual p95 calculation over 30 days: do we compute p95 on raw request latencies then aggregate, or compute per-epoch p95 and then take a weighted average? We should pick the method that is reproducible for audits.
3) Can we provide a short evidence package (sample logs + histogram snapshots) for the first 30 days? What retention/PII considerations?

Comments from Karthik (inline):
> For (2) we should compute the p95 over the full set of raw request latencies for the evaluation window. Aggregating epoch p95s can hide spikes. We'll need to store per-request latency summary histograms (not raw payloads) for audit.  — karthik_iyer

Ben: can you confirm expected p95 numbers for the EU GPU pool under the initial reserved capacity? If traffic profile stays within our assumed token distribution, the 600 ms interim p95 is conservative; we could target 500 ms as alternative. — laura

Ben (reply inline at 11:10):
> We can support a tighter interim p95 (500 ms) for the EU pool if they commit to a short ramp profile (max 2x daily burst vs baseline). Otherwise 600 ms is safer. Also recommend documenting the batch/sequence-length assumptions in the SLO appendix. — ben_carter

Marissa (reply inline at 14:03):
> I'll prepare an evidence checklist (internal-evidence-checklist.xlsx) that includes the histogram export procedure, retention notes (30 days for audit histograms), and the drive link for sharing redacted samples. — marissa_cole

Action items:
- Ben: confirm interim number to send to FinCo (500 vs 600 ms) by EOD.
- Marissa: generate the evidence checklist and sample redacted histograms.
- Karthik: finalize a short method note for contractual p95 computation (per-request set p95 over evaluation window).

I'll consolidate and send back to Alice + procurement.

Laura

Attachments: redwood-staggered-slo-proposal.pdf, internal-evidence-checklist.xlsx

Hi Alice — thanks for the patience while we aligned internally. Below is a concise version of the proposed phased SLO plan plus how we will produce evidence for compliance. If this looks OK I can add it as an addendum to the contract and loop in legal.

Proposed Phased SLO & Measurement Summary (FinCo)
1) Phase 0 — Validation (days 0–7):
- Activity: low-traffic validation, telemetry collection.
- Monitoring: 7-day rolling percentiles for operational alerts (no contractual credits).
- Evidence: histogram snapshots captured daily; short redacted samples shared to Drive.

2) Phase 1 — Interim Contractual Period (days 8–30, EU only):
- Interim targets: p50 = 100 ms, p95 = 500 ms (EU GPU pool) — we agreed to the tighter interim target provided a conservative ramp profile.
- Contractual measurement: p95 computed over the full set of request latencies across a contiguous 30-day evaluation window.
- Operational observation: 7-day rolling p95 used for alerts; any breach triggers investigation but remediation credits are capped during Phase 1 (pro-rated schedule in attached PDF).
- Carve-outs: first 10 minutes after live deploy or model switch; scheduled maintenance windows declared 48+ hours in advance.

3) Phase 2 — Standard Production Commitments (day 31+):
- Production targets: p50 = 70 ms, p95 = 450 ms (goal; will be formalized once telemetry stabilizes).
- Production measurement: standard 30-day contractual window; operational 7-day rolling for real-time monitoring.

Evidence & Auditability- We will provide a 30-day histogram export (no request payloads) and a short verification note describing the computation method (p95 over raw latencies). Retention: histogram summaries retained for 30 days for audit purposes. Marissa will share a redacted sample set via Drive.

Next steps
- Please confirm acceptance of the interim EU targets (p50=100 ms, p95=500 ms) and the phased timeline.
- If accepted, we'll attach the proposal as an addendum and include the remediation credit schedule for Phase 1.
- Proposed quick sync: Tue 13 Oct, 09:00 CET to finalize language for procurement (I can schedule).

Thanks — happy to walk through the PDF if you'd like.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
